title: GAP Waiver Premier 150 Claim Worksheet: Starting Balance
content:
**GAP Waiver Addenda, GAP Waiver Premier 150.** A total-loss or theft claim on a GAP Waiver Premier 150 addendum is a Premier worksheet claim. The starting balance its claim worksheet records is the Premier starting balance. This is the claim's balance at loss: the balance on the date of loss that the benefit starts from. The claim concerned is the latest claim reported on the addendum. Every figure is read from that claim and from the records of the addendum's own contract.

**Plans this rule governs.** On a Premier worksheet claim, the balance the benefit starts from is the Premier starting balance. On a GAP Waiver Plus 150 claim, it is the Plus starting balance. On a claim on any other plan, the benefit still starts from the scheduled balance on the date of loss, with interest accrued to the date of loss on that balance.

## Recording the starting balance

**Capability.** `record_claim_balance_at_loss_15fb7d99` records, on the GAP claim worksheet of a GAP Waiver Premier 150 addendum, the starting balance of a reported total-loss or theft claim. One call writes that figure to the claim record of the reported loss. The claim's other figures, the addendum's status and the contract stay as they are. The representative and the borrower can see the starting balance on the claim.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the representative unlocks it, then calls it.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `gap_activity_id` | the reference number of the claim record of the reported loss on the borrower's GAP waiver addendum, as returned by the GAP activity lookup for that addendum |
| `balance_at_loss_usd` | the starting balance on the date of loss, in US dollars, a number of 0.00 or more kept to 2 decimal places (rounded to the cent) |

**Return.** A confirmation text naming the claim reference number and the starting balance now recorded on it, in US dollars with 2 decimal places. Receiving this text means the figure is recorded on the claim record.

The tool writes the starting balance only. It records no decision and credits nothing to the contract.
